item.title: Version 1.2.0
item.description:
## What's new
- When AirPods or other Bluetooth headphones connect and the sound moves to them, the bezel shows their name, with an AirPods, Beats or headphones glyph. A long name wraps onto two lines. macOS shows its own banner for this too, so you'll see both. Turn it off in Settings with "Show when headphones connect". - From October 28 to November 3 the bezel dresses up for Halloween. Bats hang from the top of the bezel above a graveyard, more of them the darker the screen or the quieter the sound. Turn the volume or brightness up and they fly off. Pick the look in Settings, Harvest Moon (an amber glow) or Silhouettes, or turn seasonal bezels off with "Show seasonal bezels". - Preferences is now called Settings.
## Fixes
- Choosing Settings… from the menu bar icon now always brings the window to the front. Before, a Settings window that was already open could stay hidden behind other apps or on another Space.

item.title: Version 1.1.1
item.description:
## What's new
- On a Mac with a Touch Bar, the bezel now shows when you change volume or brightness with the Touch Bar's buttons and sliders. Until now it only appeared for the volume and brightness keys, which those Macs don't have. The Touch Bar changes the level without a key press, so ReBezel can't hide the macOS banner for these changes, and you'll see both. - A new setting in Preferences, "Show for Touch Bar controls", turns this on or off. It starts out on if your Mac has a Touch Bar. While it's on, volume and brightness changes made elsewhere, such as in Control Center, show the bezel too. - Auto-brightness and the dimming before the display sleeps don't bring up the bezel.

item.title: Version 1.1.0
item.description:
## What's new
- Hold Control while pressing a brightness key to change the brightness of an external display. This works with displays macOS itself can control (Studio Display, Pro Display XDR, LG UltraFine), not third-party monitors over DDC. ReBezel picks the display under the pointer, or the first supported one, and shows the bezel on it. With no supported display connected, the key goes to macOS as usual. - ReBezel can now update itself. Choose Check for Updates… from the menu bar icon, or leave "Automatically check for updates" on in Preferences and it checks once a day. It always asks before installing anything. - A new app icon, built for the Liquid Glass look of macOS 26, with a dark mode variant. - The app is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so macOS opens it without a Gatekeeper warning.
## Before you update
Install this version by hand from the DMG. Updates after it arrive through the app.
macOS ties Accessibility permission to the app's signature, so if you ran an earlier build you need to grant it once more in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility. Later updates keep it.
